slides.title: 5 skincare pairs that *fight* on your face
slides.sub: And one famous "don't mix" rule that's actually wrong.

slides.title: Retinol + exfoliating acids
slides.body: Both speed up cell turnover. Stacked on the same night, they often mean *redness, peeling and stinging*.
slides.fix: Alternate nights. Acids one night, retinol the next.

slides.title: Vitamin C + benzoyl peroxide
slides.body: Benzoyl peroxide can oxidize vitamin C, so the serum you paid for *does less*.
slides.fix: Vitamin C in the morning. Benzoyl peroxide at night.

slides.title: Two acids in one routine
slides.body: Layering exfoliants is the fastest way to a *tight, shiny, irritated* barrier.
slides.fix: One exfoliant per routine. Two or three times a week is plenty.

slides.title: Retinol + face scrub
slides.body: Retinoid nights leave skin more sensitive. Grains on top add *friction it doesn't need*.
slides.fix: Skip scrubs entirely on retinol nights.

slides.title: Actives + skipping SPF
slides.body: Retinoids and AHAs can make skin *more sensitive to the sun*. This is the pair most people forget.
slides.fix: SPF 30+ every morning you use them, even when it's cloudy.

slides.title: "Never mix niacinamide and vitamin C"
slides.body: The rule came from old lab tests run under heat. In today's formulas, most people use them together *without issues*.
slides.fix: Fine together. Patch test if your skin is reactive.
